extracted.intended_audience: general readers and market participants (investors, corporate compliance officers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how public companies must (and may) disclose material nonpublic information to avoid selective disclosure under SEC Regulation FD, including exceptions and acceptable dissemination venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on selective disclosure / public distribution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to certain limited exceptions, the rules generally prohibit public companies from disclosing previously nonpublic, material information to certain parties unless the information is distributed to the public first or simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation sought to stamp out selective disclosure in which some investors (often large institutional investors) received market moving information before others. To comply, companies must ensure market‑moving material information is made public (or simultaneously public) rather than provided privately to select parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insider exception / confidentiality agreement exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD does not apply to disclosures of material information to persons who are bound by duties of trust or confidence or to persons who have expressly agreed to maintain the information in confidence (including 'temporary' insiders such as outside consultants, attorneys, investment bankers, accountants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies may make selective disclosures to parties who are insiders or who have confidentiality agreements. The SEC explained that paragraph (b) of Rule 100 excludes disclosures to persons whose misuse would subject them to insider trading liability; the confidentiality agreement need not include an undertaking not to trade. Collecting a confidentiality agreement (or dealing with a party already under a duty of trust/confidence) preserves this exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of social media and web venues for disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies can use social media to disseminate information if certain requirements are met: investors' access to the chosen social media platform must not be restricted and investors must be notified about which social media will be used to disseminate information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with company websites, the chosen platform must be broadly accessible so the disclosure is effectively public. The SEC clarified this position on April 2, 2013; companies should notify investors which social media they will use for formal disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality requirement (rule applies to material information)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule only prohibits private disclosure of material information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non‑material or merely inconsequential data are not covered, but 'seemingly inconsequential data' might be consequential when combined (mosaic theory). Companies should therefore assess materiality carefully before determining whether private disclosure would violate Reg FD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public record / analyst communications exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies can inform analysts of public record information without necessarily violating the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information already of public record may be discussed privately with analysts. However, care is needed because combining public information with other nonpublic pieces could create material implications (mosaic concerns).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/applicability — covered recipients and permitted communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule applies to certain groups such as securities market professionals and shareholders, but allows the company to continue providing necessary information to business partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reg FD targets selective disclosures that advantage certain investors; it does not bar all private communications. Companies may continue routine communications with business partners and others where the rule does not apply, but should confirm whether recipients fall within the groups protected by the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal codification and reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD is codified at 17 CFR 243 and was promulgated by the SEC in August 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should refer to 17 CFR 243, the adopting release, and the SEC's Compliance and Disclosure Interpretations for authoritative text and interpretive guidance when applying Reg FD to disclosure practices (including press releases and other public statements).
